latin.735: §. VIII. Ex omnibus hactenus disputatis, & partim assertis defensísque, partim negatis ac destructis, crediderim, Lectori cuivis, etiam Wittebergensi Disputatori, Doctissimo Domino Werensdorfio abundè constare posse, tanti non esse, in quibus circa Cœnam Christi Sacram Protestantes dissentiunt, ut Dissensum ea efficere possint Fundamentalem.
latin.736: Quia Dissensus planè nullus est de vera & substantiali corporis & sanguinis Christi præsentia in Sacra Cœna, Communicantibus omnibus oblata, itemque de vera & reali, at spirituali & supernaturali, eóque tantò veriori & realiori corporis Christi Manducatione Sanguinísque Bibitione.
latin.737: Sed de sola Manducatione corporis Christi & Bibitione Sanguinis ejus, Oralibus & Corporalibus, quæ nihil quicquam prosunt; deque Manducatione Indignorum, quæ sive fiat, sive minus fiat, sitque tantum, juxta Apostolum, Manducatio panis benedicti, non corporis; Juxta Augustinum, panis qui est Domini non panis qui est Dominus, æternam iis condemnationem attrahit.
latin.738: Eóque porrò Dissensus eatenus non est de mediis salutis, Orali corporis Christi Manducatione per se Salutem nemini, nedum indigno, conferre aptâ natáque; Sed de mediis majoris duntaxat judicii & condemnationis, saltem quod ad impios attinet.
latin.739: Quapropter hoc unum restat, non, ut Reformati, agnito errore, mutent sententiam, quam nunquam habuerunt, redeántque in viam, à qua nunquam deflexerunt, & veram substantialémque corporis & sanguinis Christi in S. Cœna præsentiam, non verbis insidiose conceptis & ad homines decipiendos compositis, sed apertis & ingenuis fateantur, quam nunquam non, citra omnem tergiversationem aut hæsitantiam, fassi sunt, & in omnem æternitatem fatebuntur.
latin.740: Sed hoc unum restat, ut Clarissimus Autor, & quotquot Schisma Protestanticum fovent atque dilatant, à modis loquendi in S. Cœna, partim non revelatis, simulque contradictoriis (quales sunt: corpus Christi, cibum merè licèt Spiritualem, propriè tamen & Oraliter manducari; Itemque ab indignis propriè & oraliter manducari; Propriam etiam Manducationem, solidi licèt cibi, non esse tamen dentalem, nec gutturalem, &c.; Oralem insuper Manducationem, ore corporis naturali licèt factam, esse tamen merè Supernaturalem & Cælestem, propterea, quòd Objectum Manducationis Oralis, Corpus Christi, supernaturalis & Cœlestis tantum cibus est, Instrumento nihilominus naturali & terrestri manducandus); Partim à profanis & Religione Christiana indignis (quales sunt: Præsentiam corporis Christi per fidem, esse merum Commentum; Manducationem Spiritualem esse merè imaginariam; Fidem, meram imaginationem & cogitationem); partim denique ab invidiosis & charitatem christianam gravissimè lædentibus, quales sunt: REFORMATOS NON CREDERE, QUOD SE CREDERE SIMULANT, ILLOS ALIUD SENTIRE, ALIUD LOQUI, VERBIS INSIDIOSE CONCEPTIS ET AD DECIPIENDOS HOMINES COMPOSITIS, PRÆSENTIAM CORPORIS CHRISTI IN S. CŒNA FATERI — toti abstineant.
latin.741: Et Propositionem hanc suam Conditionatam: Si reverà hoc crederent, quod se credere simulant Reformati, nempe Corpus & sanguinem Christi, verè & Substantialiter adesse in S. Cœna, non modo plurimum decessurum esse momento Controversiæ, sed & munitum iri aditum ad ea quæ restant capita facilius componenda, in hanc absolutam & categoricam convertant, quam vel charitas Christiana, per omnia propemodum attributa sua essentialia, Apostolo 1. Cor. XIII. descripta, ab iis efflagitat: Reformati credunt proculdubio, quod credere se dicunt, nempe corpus & sanguinem Christi verè & substantialiter adesse in Sacra Cœna, sicque non modo deest omne momentum Controversiæ, sed & munitus aditus ad ea quæ restant pauciora minoraque inter Evangelicos capita facilius componenda.
latin.742: Aditum itaque hunc jam tum munitum, muniat ampliùs utraque pars. Fundamentalem Consensum Evangelicorum, i. e. Lutheranos inter & Reformatos, omnium oculos perstringentem, apertè fateatur; De Dissensu qui restat, minus fundamentali, placidè inter se conferendo, Veritatem revelatam piè meditando, scrutando, nullum, extra Revelationem, ad fidem & salutem necessarium Dogma constituendo, errantes infirmósque in fide tolerando, pro istis, ceu fidei consanguineis, apud Deum precibus intercedendo, minuat éque medio tollere studeat; Omnes utriusque partis Doctores memores identidem sint loquendi veritatem in charitate, ut sic utriusque partis cœtus omnes in sincera charitate mutua adolescant in eum, qui est caput, nempe Christus, ex quo totum corpus congruenter coagmentatum succrescit, donec tandem singuli perveniamus ad unam per omnia fidem & Cognitionem filii DEI, perfectíque evadamus ad mensuram perfectæ Christianitatis, verè sic pacifici & filii DEI nuncupandi Festúmque Jubilare, cum Ecclesia & Universitate Marchica, mox celebrandum, sempiternâ Solennitate continuaturi in DEI SOLIUS GLORIAM.

pass_a.735: §. VIII. From all things hitherto disputed, and partly asserted and defended, partly denied and destroyed, I should believe it can abundantly be clear to any Reader, even to the Wittenberg Disputant, the most learned Domine Werensdorf, that those things in which Protestants dissent about Christ’s Sacred Supper are not of such weight that they can make the Dissensus Fundamental.
pass_a.736: Because there is plainly no Dissensus about the true and substantial presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Sacred Supper, offered to all Communicants, and likewise about the true and real, yet spiritual and supernatural — and so much the truer and realer — Eating of Christ’s body and Drinking of the Blood.
pass_a.737: But only about Oral and Corporal Eating of Christ’s body and Drinking of his Blood, which profit nothing whatever; and about the Eating of the Unworthy, which whether it happen or less happen, is only, according to the Apostle, Eating of blessed bread, not of the body; according to Augustine, bread which is of the Lord, not bread which is the Lord — and draws eternal condemnation to them.
pass_a.738: And so further the Dissensus is not thus far about means of salvation — Oral Eating of Christ’s body being by itself apt and born to confer Salvation on no one, much less on the unworthy — but only about means of greater judgment and condemnation, at least as concerns the Impious.
pass_a.739: Wherefore this one thing remains — not that the Reformed, error acknowledged, change a sentence they never held, and return to a way from which they never deflected, and confess with open and ingenuous words the true and substantial presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Holy Supper — not with words insidiously conceived and composed to deceive men — which presence they have never not confessed, without all tergiversation or hesitation, and will confess to all eternity.
pass_a.740: But this one thing remains: that the most distinguished Author, and as many as foster and widen the Protestant Schism, wholly abstain from modes of speaking in the Holy Supper partly unrevealed and at once contradictory (such as: Christ’s body, food though merely Spiritual, yet properly and Orally eaten; and likewise properly and orally eaten by the unworthy; also that proper Eating, of solid food though it be, is yet not dental nor guttural, &c.; moreover that Oral Eating, though done with the body’s natural mouth, is yet merely Supernatural and Heavenly, because the Object of Oral Eating, Christ’s Body, is only supernatural and Heavenly food, nevertheless to be eaten with a natural and earthly Instrument); partly from profane and Christian-Religion-unworthy sayings (such as: presence of Christ’s body by faith is a mere Fiction; Spiritual Eating is merely imaginary; Faith is mere imagination and thought); and finally partly from invidious sayings most gravely wounding Christian charity — such as: THE REFORMED DO NOT BELIEVE WHAT THEY PRETEND TO BELIEVE, THEY THINK ONE THING AND SAY ANOTHER, AND WITH WORDS INSIDIOUSLY CONCEIVED AND COMPOSED TO DECEIVE MEN CONFESS THE PRESENCE OF CHRIST’S BODY IN THE HOLY SUPPER.
pass_a.741: And let them convert this Conditional Proposition of theirs — If the Reformed truly believed what they pretend to believe, namely that Christ’s Body and blood are truly and Substantially present in the Holy Supper, not only would much of the Controversy’s moment depart, but also the way would be fortified to composing more easily the remaining heads — into this absolute and categorical one, which even Christian charity, by nearly all its essential attributes described by the Apostle in 1 Cor. 13, demands of them: The Reformed beyond doubt believe what they say they believe, namely that Christ’s body and blood are truly and substantially present in the Sacred Supper — and so not only is every moment of Controversy wanting, but also the way is fortified to composing more easily the fewer and lesser remaining heads among Evangelicals.
pass_a.742: Let therefore both parties further fortify this way already then fortified. Let the Fundamental Consensus of Evangelicals — i.e. between Lutherans and Reformed — striking all eyes, be openly confessed; concerning the Dissensus that remains, less fundamental, by conferring placidly among themselves, piously meditating and searching the revealed Truth, constituting no Dogma necessary to faith and salvation outside Revelation, tolerating those erring and weak in faith, interceding for them before God as faith’s kin — let it be lessened and studied to be taken from the midst; Let all Doctors of both parties be mindful again and again of speaking the truth in love, that so all assemblies of both parties may grow in mutual sincere charity into him who is the head, namely Christ, from whom the whole body fitly framed grows, until at last we each arrive at one faith through all and Knowledge of the Son of GOD, and become perfect to the measure of perfect Christianity, truly thus to be called peaceful and sons of GOD — and the Jubilee Feast soon to be celebrated with the Marchic Church and University, to be continued with sempiternal Solemnity unto the GLORY OF GOD ALONE.

735: §.VIII: from all disputed so far — asserted or denied — it should be clear even to Wittenberg’s Werensdorf.
Protestant disagreements about the Sacred Supper are not of such weight as to make the dissensus faith-fundamental.
736: There is plainly no dissensus on true substantial presence of body and blood in the Supper, offered to all communicants.
Nor on true real eating and drinking that is spiritual and supernatural — and so much the truer and realer.
737: The fight is only over Oral and Corporal eating and drinking, which profit nothing.
And over Indignorum eating — which, whether it happens or not, is only blessed bread per Paul, bread of the Lord not bread the Lord per Augustine, and draws condemnation.
738: So the dissensus is not about means of salvation — Oral eating by itself saves no one, least of all the unworthy.
It is about means of greater judgment and condemnation, at least for the Impious.
739: What remains is not that the Reformed ‘admit error’ and return to a path they never left.
They have always, without tergiversation, confessed true substantial presence in open words — and will forever.
740: What remains: the Author and all who widen Protestant schism must drop unrevealed, contradictory Supper-speech (spiritual food orally chewed; Indigni oral eating; non-dental solid eating; natural mouth yet merely heavenly, &c.).
Drop also profane charges (faith-presence a fiction; spiritual eating imaginary; faith mere thought) and the invidious claim that the Reformed pretend belief while saying another thing to deceive.
741: Convert their conditional — “if the Reformed really believed substantial presence, controversy would shrink and the rest would compose easier” — into the absolute charity demands (1 Cor 13).
The Reformed beyond doubt believe what they say: body and blood truly and substantially present — so the main moment of controversy is gone, and the way to lesser remaining heads is open.
742: Both sides should fortify that already-open way: confess the fundamental Evangelic consensus (Lutheran–Reformed) in the open; treat the lesser remaining dissent with calm conference, revealed truth, no extra-revelatory necessary dogmas, tolerance, and prayer for weaker kin.

Doctors of both sides: speak the truth in love, grow into Christ the head, unto one faith and knowledge of the Son — peaceful sons of God — and keep the coming Marchic Jubilee in everlasting solemnity unto the GLORY OF GOD ALONE. Annotatio VI closes.

notes.736: Agreement on substantial + spiritual real eating.

notes.742: Consensus; truth in love; Jubilee; Annot. VI end.
